goldParcelRead.falsifier3: FIRED. The dispatch pre-registered exactly this outcome: 'If 48209:97658 still says not-cut-over after a successful apply, the slate and the cells are not the same gate and that is a bigger finding than this row.' The apply is real and verified (store write confirmed by direct SQL read-back; gate verdict confirmed PASS by direct gate-rail-cli read) -- this is not a failed apply. get_smart_site's node-depth response is explicitly `mode: baked-facet-intel-v1`, `source: baked-snapshot`, and both calls returned the IDENTICAL runId/bakedAt timestamp, which predates the apply by several hours. The most-evidenced explanation: this MCP surface serves a periodically-baked snapshot rather than dereferencing parcel_record_cell / parcel_gate_verdict live per request, and no bake has run for this parcel since before this lane's apply. This conflicts with the canon preamble's own ledger-as-serving-path rule ('one reader in hauska-engine/services/retrieval-api walks gated cells and dereferences atoms and every surface and the Hauska MCP catalog consume it') if that rule is meant to describe get_smart_site specifically -- reconciling which is bigger than this row and not attempted here. No re-bake was triggered; triggering one was not authorized this wave ('Deploy anything further' is explicitly out of scope) and the mechanism that would do so was not identified in the time available.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: EARNED_CELL_KINDS = ['value','absent-verified','refused'] only -- 'not-applicable' does NOT count as earned for evaluateRailGate's liveness check. A rail whose only earned-looking cells are all not-applicable (e.g. every unincorporated parcel in a county) still reads excludedDeclaredAhead if every in-city cell is unaccounted. Verified 2026-09-15 via src/lib/parcel-record-engine/cell-state.js.

gate-rail-cli.mjs's own liveness pre-scan (loadProgramWideLiveRailKeys, RAIL_LIVENESS_SQL) is the expensive part on a cold call and can be computed once and passed via --declared-ahead to every subsequent call in the same session -- cut repeat calls from ~70s+ to ~17s each.

parcel-setback-cells.mjs's --city filter has no county boundary: CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL matches city_name against ALL of IN_SCOPE_COUNTIES, not the caller's intended single county. A city name shared across counties (Austin, San Marcos, Buda, Creedmoor, Niederwald, Uhland all cross Hays/Travis/Caldwell lines in this program's six counties) silently re-reads (but, thanks to the unaccounted-only write guard, does not re-write) the other county's parcels too. Safe by construction for a re-run, but makes a --city-scoped dry-run or apply preview misleading unless independently reconciled per county.

get_smart_site depth=node returns mode:'baked-facet-intel-v1' with a shared runId/bakedAt for the whole payload -- confirmed by direct A/B read (same runId both times) that it does NOT re-dereference parcel_record_cell live per call for at least the setbackRulesFact path, contradicting a plain reading of the ledger-as-serving-path canon rule. Worth checking before trusting any get_smart_site read as evidence that a just-landed write reached the customer surface -- verify the underlying store and gate directly instead, or confirm the bake has re-run.

Why does get_smart_site's bake not re-run promptly after a parcel_record_cell write that flips its gate verdict to pass? Is there a bake job/cadence this program expects to trigger it, and if so what triggers it and how long is the normal lag? Next context should check for a bake/publish job in hauska-engine's services/retrieval-api or a related repo before assuming this is broken vs. merely not-yet-triggered.
